# onpager_team (Resource)

Manage an OnPager team and its active state.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "onpager_team" "example" {
  name = "Operations"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Nonempty name without leading or trailing whitespace. Unique case-insensitively within the tenant, including inactive records.

### Optional

- `active` (Boolean) Whether the object is active. Defaults to `true`. Changes disable or reactivate the existing UUID. Disabled objects remain in state; refresh and import never reactivate them.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Stable nonzero canonical lowercase OnPager UUID.

## Import

Import using the team UUID, rather than its name or slug. A later apply
reconciles `active`; set `active = false` to keep an imported team inactive.

Use an `import` block:

```terraform
import {
  to = onpager_team.example
  id = "11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111"
}
```

Or use the CLI:

```shell
terraform import onpager_team.example 11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111
```

## Lifecycle

Destroy disables the team, preserving its UUID, history and links. Disabling
also disables owned services, alert filters, escalation rules and explicitly
owned service accounts, and revokes those accounts' keys. Use credentials
independent of the team being retired. API failures retain state.

Externally disabled teams remain managed. Reactivation preserves memberships and
configuration; disabled children and revoked keys are not restored. Manage each
child's desired active state separately. An inactive team's name remains
reserved; import its existing UUID to manage it again.

Team writes use the unversioned API without revision preconditions.

## Permissions

Creation, disable and reactivation require tenant-scoped `teams.create`,
`teams.disable` and `teams.reactivate`, respectively. Read and name updates
require `teams.read` and `teams.update` for the selected team or at tenant scope.
Creating a team does not grant membership or a role assignment.
